issue.title: Camera hand tracking as a position hint (Phase 0b)
issue.body:
## Context
Phase 0b (docs/PLAN.md section 5) tests real position hints instead of ideal ones. The phone camera is the free option: if a hand-tracking model can say roughly which fret the fretting hand is at, the measured gain (43% to up to 89% right string) needs no hardware at all. Frets 5–12 are 2–3 cm apart, so the estimate only needs to be within about 1–2 frets.

## What to do
- Add `experiments/camera-hint/`: a script that takes a video of someone playing (phone on a stand, neck in view) and writes a hint CSV of `t,fret` rows, for example every 0.25 s.
- Suggested approach: MediaPipe Hands (or similar) for the fretting-hand landmarks, plus a simple neck calibration (the user clicks the nut and the 12th fret on the first frame; fret positions follow from the 2^(-n/12) spacing rule).
- Report how far the estimate is from the truth on a few clips you recorded yourself, with the frets you actually played.
- The hint CSV should match the format of the `--hints` issue (#3) so the two plug together. If that issue is not merged yet, use `t,fret` with a header.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `python camera_hint.py video.mp4 --out hints.csv` runs on a phone video
- [ ] A README in the folder: setup, calibration steps, the dependencies, and the accuracy you measured (median fret error)
- [ ] Dependencies live in that folder's own `requirements.txt`, not the phone-audio one
- [ ] No recordings committed (keep them out of git or link to them)

## Pointers
- `docs/PLAN.md` section 5 (Phase 0b exit criterion: right string ≥ 85%)
- `docs/phone-audio-experiment.md` ("Feedback", point 3)
- `experiments/phone-audio/fretmap.py` (`assign()` reads `note["around"]`)

## Difficulty
Hard. Computer vision; needs a guitar and a phone or webcam.

issue.title: Lease long-poll holds a threadpool thread per waiting worker
issue.body:
## Context
Workers long-poll `POST /workers/{id}/lease?wait=` (up to 25 s). The handler in `backend/app/routers/workers.py` is a sync `def` that loops `time.sleep(LONG_POLL_STEP)` and re-queries until a job appears or the deadline passes. FastAPI runs sync handlers in a shared threadpool (about 40 threads by default), so every waiting worker holds a thread for up to 25 s. The code comment says this stops scaling past about 30 workers per process; after that, every other sync endpoint (job submit, balance, dashboard calls) queues behind idle long-polls.

## What to do
Make waiting long-polls stop holding threadpool threads. Two possible approaches; propose yours in the issue before a large PR:
- Make `lease` `async def`, run each short DB attempt (`_try_lease`) in the threadpool and `await asyncio.sleep(...)` between attempts, with a fresh session or a clean transaction for each attempt.
- Or wake waiters with Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` when a job is queued, keeping polling on SQLite.

Behaviour must not change: same lease semantics, `204` on timeout, SKIP LOCKED leasing on Postgres, and the per-route rate limit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test opens more concurrent long-polls than the threadpool size (for example 60 with `wait` set) and shows that an unrelated request (for example `GET /jobs`) still answers quickly while they wait.
- [ ] The existing suites pass on SQLite, and on Postgres with `TEST_DATABASE_URL` if you can run Docker (see `AGENTS.md`), including the lease race and SKIP LOCKED tests.
- [ ] The shortcut comment on `lease` is removed or updated.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including the reverse-order runs.

## Pointers
- `backend/app/routers/workers.py` (`lease`, `_try_lease`, `LONG_POLL_STEP`)
- `backend/app/database.py` (session setup), `backend/app/ratelimit.py`
- `backend/tests/test_concurrency.py`, `backend/tests/test_e2e.py`
- `worker/src/reserve_my_tokens_worker/polling_client.py` (client side of `?wait=`)

## Difficulty
Hard. Concurrency, SQLAlchemy sessions and FastAPI's threadpool.
